key_insight: An evaluator-guided large language model search can discover quantum circuit designs that outperform the state of the art in both Toffoli and qubit cost across diverse tasks.
engineering_relevance: This points to a practical co-design workflow for reducing quantum resource overhead in algorithms where reversibility makes manual optimization especially difficult.
method: LLMs propose candidate quantum circuit designs.
An independent evaluator verifies correctness and scores resource use.
An evolutionary loop iterates over tasks in computation, chemistry, optimization, simulation, and number theory.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmark tasks, seven showed significant reductions in both Toffoli and qubit counts, and the eighth produced a new reversible prime-field modular inversion architecture.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the evaluator and benchmark definitions, so gains may not transfer directly to hardware-constrained or differently specified quantum workloads.
paper_title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
